To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the identification of HCN in the 2-4 µm spectrum of carbon stars has been extended to the HCN ν _{1} +ν _{3} band, and that HNC has been identified for the first time in the 2 µm spectrum of a carbon star.
the HNC molecule has a significant effect on stellar atmosphere temperature, density and opacities and can be detected in the ISO spectra of carbon stars.
HCN and HCN absorption is required to explain the observed spectra of WZ Cas and that this absorption is not well explained by a single temperature, single density model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of HCN/HNC in the 2-4 µm region of the ISO SWS spectra of carbon stars, and the determination of effective temperatures and log(NC/HNC) from these observations.
the development of new models for carbon star atmospheres, the calculation of synthetic spectra, and the identification of HCN/HNC features in the spectra of carbon stars.
understanding the formation of molecules in carbon stars and the role of HCN and its isotope in the chemical evolution of the interstellar medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HNC/HCN ratio is not known and cannot be reliably determined from the observations of any one object.
the HCN and HCN lines are not observed in the 2-4 µm region.
the results presented in this thesis provide a strong indication that HNC is present in stellar atmospheres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model spectra and fits are a significant advance in the modelling of carbon star spectra.
the HNC lines are not as strong as HCN lines in the 3.5 µm region but they are more important in the 2 µm region.
the HNC lines are important for the carbon star atmospheres.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that the presence of HNC in the atmospheres of C stars has a significant effect on the temperature, density, and optical depth of stellar atmosphere models, and that it is necessary to use the complete HCN/HNC linelist to fit observations in the 3 µm region.
HNC is a significant contributor to the chemistry of the carbon stars.
HNC should be included in future model carbon star atmospheres.
